articles.title: What Abstraction Does React Introduce?
articles.excerpt: JavaScript could already update the DOM. So why did we need React? In my previous post, we discussed the history of Web UI and how it evolved from HTML to React. But there are many misconceptions abou…
articles.body: JavaScript could already update the DOM. So why did we need React? In my previous post, we discussed the history of Web UI and how it evolved from HTML to React. But there are many misconceptions about React. One of them is that React removes DOM manipulation. That’s not the proper way to understand it. Instead, React abstracts DOM manipulation. So, what is abstraction? The bigger picture of React's abstraction is where you describe UI declaratively as a function of application state, organize UI into components, and then let React handle the synchronization between that description and the React rendering environment. That is about the overall abstraction, which abstracts many underlying tasks. Let's understand that. Abstractions 1.

articles.title: I can't ask my old team lead why anymore, so I built a séance
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine. A month ago my team lead left. He was the one who knew why our code is shaped the way it is: why one p…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine . A month ago my team lead left. He was the one who knew why our code is shaped the way it is: why one piece is split from another, why a check lives here and not there, why a decision that looks wrong was actually right. More than once since then I have hit one of those decisions, opened a chat to ask him, and stopped halfway through typing. He has moved on. It felt wrong to pull him back into code he no longer owns, and there was nobody else to ask. git blame did not help. It showed me the last person who touched the file, not the person who decided why it exists.

articles.title: Black October: 9 AI Dev Platforms Were Breached. Rotate Your Keys Today
articles.excerpt: TL;DR: In October 2026, at least nine AI developer platforms disclosed security incidents, according to a Wiz research post published on October 30. The common thread is that attackers went after stor…
articles.body: TL;DR: In October 2026, at least nine AI developer platforms disclosed security incidents, according to a Wiz research post published on October 30 . The common thread is that attackers went after stored environment variables, especially the ones that unlock AI models. Stolen keys were tested within about 30 minutes and later resold. If you have an OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock or similar key sitting in a hosting or dev platform, rotate it today. Then put a spend cap on it and narrow its scope. There's a checklist below. Any other month, one AI platform breach would have been the security story of the week. This month there were nine, and Wiz's researchers had to point out that hardly anyone was connecting them. They called it "Black October".

articles.excerpt: It's still unknown how attackers got access to Anthropic's verified Cursor account.
articles.body: An official extension for Anthropic’s Claude model was backdoored and threatened as many as 5,000 developers' machines, multiple sources reported Friday. Anthropic so far has yet to warn customers of the incident. The compromised package was a VS Code extension available in the marketplace of Cursor, a maker of AI-assisted developer tools, the company said Friday. The malicious version, 2.1.313, subsequently affected “at most 5,000 users,” presumably when they either downloaded it or their systems automatically fetched and installed it. Anthropic pushed version 2.1.314 several hours after the previous version became available on Cursor, according to independent researcher Kevin Beaumont.

articles.body: Our time on our "space mission" underwater was coming to an end, and I felt like what I imagine an astronaut on the International Space Station (ISS) must feel before returning to Earth. On one hand, you are excited to return to your home and loved ones, as well as to fresh food and normal hygiene. On the other, you know you will miss your crew and the incredible experience of being in space. While my SEA STAR crew and I had not left Earth during our mission, we were separated from the surface of our home planet for five days. All we saw was a green alien water world surrounding us. We did this to live and work like astronauts on the ISS .

articles.title: India launches next-gen navigation satellite to orbit (video)
articles.excerpt: India launched the NVS-03 navigation satellite to orbit today (Oct. 30) atop a GSLV rocket. It was the fourth orbital launch from Indian soil so far this year.
articles.body: India bolstered its homegrown satellite-navigation system today (Oct. 30). A GSLV Mark II rocket launched the nation's NVS-03 satellite from Satish Dhawan Space Centre today at 2:21 p.m. EDT (1821 GMT and 11:51 p.m. India Standard Time). Everything went well: The rocket deployed NVS-03 into geostationary transfer orbit as planned, officials with the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) announced on X about 30 minutes after liftoff. An Indian GSLV Mark II rocket launches the NVS-03 navigation satellite on Oct. 30, 2026. (Image credit: ISRO) NVS-03 is the third next-gen satellite that India has launched for the Navigation with Indian Constellation (NavIC), its version of the United States' Global Positioning System ( GPS ).

articles.title: 5 horror franchises that went to space... and one that absolutely should have but didn't
articles.excerpt: In space, no one can hear you scream, a bit like the empty theater screens that some horror franchise's final installments limp. But there are still some real gems among the space-based frightfests.
articles.body: In space, no one can hear you scream... not unlike in the empty theater screens that aging horror franchises play to when the lustre has gone and their final installments limp to the public. It is perhaps little wonder that some horror franchises go to space to die... or take long breaks, at least. In celebration of Halloween , we're running down some horror franchises that made the journey to the final frontier, resulting in films that range from the sublime and outrageously campy fun to just pure awful. Absent from the list are space horror movies that have space baked into their natural fabric. So no Event Horizon, no Alien, and no Critters 4 (they were aliens, so they just went back to space; that doesn't count). 1.
